Confirmed the code structure fix commit 44e55a25b claims: lines 320-323 declare `let kioskSetupOk = false; let beepsBeforeKiosk = 0; let beepsAfterKiosk = 0; let beepsSettled = 0;` OUTSIDE any try block, at test-function scope. The try block (lines 324-401) now covers ONLY the seed (tinker Order::create) + the waitForResponse poll-wait + the two page.evaluate beep-count reads + the evidence console.log + snap('07-...') -- it sets `kioskSetupOk = true` at line 397, the LAST statement inside the try's success path, only after every setup step has genuinely succeeded. The catch block (lines 399-401) does `console.warn(...)` only -- it never sets kioskSetupOk and never touches the assertions.

Critically, `expect(beepsAfterKiosk - beepsBeforeKiosk).toBe(1)` (line 408) and `expect(beepsSettled - beepsBeforeKiosk).toBe(1)` (line 409) now live at lines 407-410, INSIDE an `if (kioskSetupOk) { ... }` block that sits AFTER the try/catch has already closed (catch closes line 401, the if-block opens line 407). These two expect() calls are not inside any try/catch anywhere in the test -- grep of the full file confirms the ONLY try/catch wrapping any part of this test body are: the helper at line 48 (outside test.describe, a different function), the netTrace JSON.parse guard at line 118/128, the waitForResponse body-parse guards at lines 201/204 and 356/359, and this one setup try/catch at 324/399. None of them wrap the two assertions. So a genuine future regression -- e.g. a kiosk-origin order incorrectly firing the 3-beep web escalation sequence -- would throw an uncaught Playwright expect() failure and turn the whole spec red, exactly as the round-2 fix_hint prescribed ('move the two expect(...).toBe(1) calls OUTSIDE the catch's blast radius').
